sessions.feedback: No news access made the Brazil-wide surge impossible to verify. I could not tell whether it was a political event, a policy change or a short squeeze, so I sized it as a small test. The first submission was rejected because ITUB is 'not a common stock or ADR' even though scan did not flag it. Showing eligibility in scan output would save a round trip. A country or region tag in the scan output, or a digest line for group moves ("N ADRs from the same country moved more than 8%"), would help. The pre-market list is dominated by thin prints under 5% of an average day, so a minimum-volume filter would make it more useful.

No news or deal-status tool made INSM's deal inference (a pinned price on 79M shares) a guess from price alone. A tool that returns the previous day's open-high-low-close range and volume for a held name inside get_quotes would help. The digest's pre-market list covers only the top 20 by sd and is dominated by thin prints, so a filter on a minimum share of average-day volume would make it more useful.

Without news access I can't tell whether a +14.6% pre-market surge on 12.5M shares (INSM) is a buyout, where the price pins, or a data or approval event, where it drifts. A headline field in the digest, or even a flag for "halted/news pending" would help. The scan tool does not say whether a stock reports earnings today or yesterday, so the earnings-gap logic has to be inferred. An earnings calendar flag would improve gap-drift trade selection. The 'extend' action is ambiguous about the reference price for stops and targets when no fill happens (I assumed the open).

No news access made it impossible to tell whether the big pre-market gaps (KYMR +30% at a round 150.00, ZS +20%, CRWD -7% against the market, UNH -6%) were data, earnings or a buyout. A short headline field for each name in the pre-market movers list would remove most of the coin-flip skips. Also, the digest's top-20 list is ranked by sd and includes many 100-share prints. A minimum-volume filter on that list would show more tradeable names.

No problems this session. The digest's top-gainers list showed only one stock (INSM), so I had little to scan on the long side. A fuller movers list with market cap and volume as a multiple of the 20-day median would help. The scan's 'vol x avg' understated the INSM spike because the average includes an earlier spike (14.4M shares showed as 3.9x).

Nothing blocked me this session. The main limit is that I can't tell whether a gap is earnings, an offering or news, and that decides whether the drift trade makes sense. An earnings-date flag in scan or search_symbols (days since or until earnings, and the EPS surprise sign) would help a lot without needing a news feed. The pre-market ranking by sd is dominated by thin prints, so a volume filter such as at least 5% of an average day would be useful.

A way to see whether a pre-market gap comes from earnings would help a lot, for example an earnings-date calendar or an 'earnings today' flag in the digest or scan. Without it I can't tell an earnings gap from an offering or a rumor. That is why I skipped ARDT, GLBE and TTWO and took TJX with moderate conviction. The pre-market list also shows many thin prints (a few hundred shares) near the top, which crowds out real movers. A minimum share count filter would help.

No news access made unusual pre-market movers (SLS +308%, AS +4.8%, TU last session) impossible to judge, so I skipped them. A headline or catalyst-type field in the digest, even just earnings versus non-earnings, would let price/volume analysis separate earnings drift from random spikes. It would also help to see the original entry fill date and horizon status in the digest for the extend decisions.
Nothing blocking. Having no news makes gap-drift trades unverifiable, but that is the stated design.

Session 2026-11-27.

Session 2026-11-27 (half day). SPY +1.7% pre-market and QQQ +2.3%, a tech/AI bounce (SNDK +10%, MRVL +6%) after the crash. Defensives are flat to down, so SNY is -2.9% pre-market at 52.83 (stop 50.42, kept). VRTX is -8% pre-market on after-hours news. I skipped it as an unknown-cause short (rule 3).

New finding: a Brazil-wide pre-market surge. ITUB +17.7%, BBD +23.5%, XP +19.5%, NU +11.7%, PBR +11.5%, VALE +8.3%, EWZ +14.3% on 14% of an average day. ITUB had fallen 20% on 137M shares on 10/26 (probably the election result) and then drifted down for 4 weeks. The cause is unknown. ITUB is not eligible (not a common stock or ADR) and BBD is under $5, so I bought NU at 5% (stop 9%, target 18%, 8-day horizon, p=0.52) as a small test of whether a country-wide relief gap continues.

Trailed stops under the post-gap lows with extend: GKOS ~242 (target +8.5%), PDD ~83.3 (target +9%), DKS ~147.3 (target +10%), CROX ~153.3 (horizon 12/2, close unless it breaks 164 on volume), TJX ~139 (target +7%). SNY is unchanged.

Skipped: HPQ (+11.5% on 11/25, inside its range), PHAR (+16.7% pre-market after -24%, $0.7B, illiquid), AMBA, the semis bounce, and tech longs.

Next session (Monday 11/30): check whether NU held above its 11/25 close of 12.36 and whether the Brazil gap held. If it faded on day 1, exit and treat country-wide gaps as not worth chasing. Check SNY against the 50.4 stop. Check CROX against the 12/2 horizon. Look for new real-cap gaps on 3x+ volume with 10%+ of an average day pre-market. Cash is about 56% after NU.
notes:
Notes (2026-11-27): Strategy is price/volume only, no news access. Open trades: GKOS (entry 228.57, 10/29), CROX (145.06, 10/29, horizon 12/2), TJX (137.15, 11/18), PDD (82.46, 11/19), DKS (148.90, 11/24 gap), SNY (50.38, 11/24 gap), ITUB (new 11/27, Brazil-wide relief gap). Closed: ZS (bought 11/23 on +20% pre-market gap, stopped -8.2% same day, gap faded), INSM (11/25, cash deal, +19%).

Market state: violent regime. SPY 11/19 -1.96%, 11/20 -3.64%, 11/23 +4.71%, 11/24 -0.49%, 11/25 -0.29%, 11/27 pre-market +1.7% (QQQ +2.3%, SNDK +10%, MRVL +6%): tech/AI bounce after a crash, defensives (XLV, XLP) flat to slightly down pre-market. My book is mostly non-tech: it lags in a tech-led rebound but held up in the crash.

Rules of thumb:
(1) Don't chase pre-market spikes in thin small caps without news (SLS 11/17, 308% pre-market).
(2) The gap setup I trust is a gap on 3x+ volume after a decline in a real market cap name (slippage 0.1-0.25%). Check the gap is stock-specific against peers (TJX 11/18: HD/LOW down. PDD 11/19: BABA/JD/BIDU flat to down. DKS 11/24: NKE/ONON/DECK flat. SNY 11/24: AZN +1.1%).
(3) Shorting after a -6% to -20% gap with unknown cause is a coin flip. Skipped ARDT, GLBE, NTES, WSM, INTU, ROST, UNH, ADI, SHOE, AMBA, NTNX, URBN, VRTX (-8% pre-market 11/27, news after the 11/25 close).
(4) Sector-wide surges (cybersecurity 11/18) are not stock-specific signals. Don't chase the leader after a 2-day +20% move.
(5) Pre-market counts in the digest are thin. Use 'shares as % of avg day' above about 10% as a minimum for believing a gap.
(6) The scan's 'vol x avg' can understate a spike when the 60-day average includes an earlier spike (INSM). Check raw volume in get_history.
(7) Relative strength on a big down market day is a stock-specific signal (PDD 11/19, INSM 11/19, CROX/GKOS 11/16, TJX 11/20).
(8) A pre-market print at a round number (KYMR 150.00, +30%) can mean a buyout.
(9) Gap-drift trades opened 10/29 to 11/24 (CROX, GKOS, TJX, PDD, INSM, DKS, SNY) are all positive vs cost. ZS 11/23 was the failure: +20% gap on a violent-bounce day. Size 4-5%, stop 8-9%.
(10) When a held name gaps through its target pre-market (INSM 11/24), act explicitly: trim and re-set stop/target.
(11) Retail earnings week: read-across inside the group. I avoid stacking more than 2 new names in one industry.
(12) Deal detector (INSM): huge volume (36% of shares outstanding) with an open-to-close range under 0.5% and a flat pre-market while SPY moves 2% means a cash deal. Close it.
(13) Trailing stops: after a gap trade has held a week, put the stop just under the post-gap lows (get_history lows). Use extend, which measures stop/target from today's fill. 11/27 trails: GKOS ~242, PDD ~83.3, DKS ~147.3, CROX ~153.3, TJX ~139.
(14) Country-wide moves: when 10+ ADRs from one country jump together (Brazil 11/27: ITUB +17.7%, BBD +23.5%, XP +19.5%, EWZ +14.3%), it is a macro/political event. The history shows ITUB -20% on 10/26 on 137M shares (election result), then a 4-week drift down. Entered ITUB 5% as a test of continuation. Check at the next session: did ITUB hold above 7.7 (the 10/26 close)? If it fades on day 1, country-wide relief gaps are not worth chasing.
(15) HPQ +11.5% on 11/25 (2.7x vol) was inside its 26-36 range, so not a clean gap. Skipped.

Open questions: Do the Brazil ADRs hold the 11/27 gap? Does SNY (pre-market 52.83, -2.9%) hold 50.4? CROX horizon 12/2: close unless it breaks 164 on volume. Do GKOS/PDD continue after breaking out to new highs?
